title: NVIDIA / auto-ontology
description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows. [2,679 stars today]

title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
description:
arXiv:2611.05393v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models perform strongly on standard medical QA but degrade on harder reasoning tasks, where multi-agent debate often fails to beat strong single-model prompting. We argue that a key limitation is that existing systems select experts and retrieve knowledge from the question alone, rather than from gaps that emerge during reasoning. title: Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?
description: I'm curious how people on HN are using AI day to day, and came up with a list of questions I thought could be interesting to know. No need to answer every question of course, just wanted to get a gut feel how people are using AI. 1) What AI subscriptions are you personally paying for? title: How Do Artificial Agents Make Decisions in Light of Visual Data?
description:
arXiv:2611.05671v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated significant advances in reasoning with visual data, which is particularly important given that much of human knowledge is encoded visually in scientific articles and other sources. description:

Abstract: Organizations accumulate evidence in conversations, documents, decisions and relationships, but they act on interpretations: judgements assembled from several observations, resting on assumptions, and revised as circumstances change. title: PAYWORTHY: Can LLMs Predict Which Freelance Jobs an AI Agent Will Complete?
description:
arXiv:2611.05759v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Before an AI agent takes on a paid job, someone has to judge whether it is likely to succeed. We test whether frontier language models can make this call before any attempt. We propose PAYWORTHY which contains 1{,}494 real freelance job postings, sampled from 18.8M postings made between 2020 and 2026 on a freelancing platform. title: Robots in the City: Persona-Based Perceptions of Urban Robots
description:
arXiv:2611.05954v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Pedestrians increasingly encounter robots in urban public spaces without interacting with them, but how robots change the perceived safety of a street remains unclear. We examine how robot presence and type affect perceived safety across urban contexts. description:

Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have established human-agent collaboration as a promising paradigm for data science. title: Dull, Dirty, Dangerous? Working Conditions and the Limits of Occupational AI Exposure
description:
arXiv:2611.06888v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Automation is often justified as relief from dull, dirty, and dangerous work. I examine how these conditions relate to occupational AI exposure using 21 O*NET items across 754 US occupations. description:
arXiv:2604.01650v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Smell's connections with food, memory, and social experience have motivated researchers to bring olfaction into interactive systems. Multimodal AI opens new possibilities for generating smells from natural language, yet it remains unclear whether pretrained models encode sufficient olfactory knowledge to translate language into perceptible compositions. description:

Abstract: Textual information is ubiquitous in real-world time series datasets, appearing as news, reports, and annotations that hold key predictive signals not deducible from numerical history alone. title: C-GRPO: Conformal Group Relative Policy Optimization
description:
arXiv:2611.05591v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reasoning-oriented language model training increasingly relies on multiple on-policy rollouts, but standard Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) uses a fixed group size, wasting compute on easy prompts and under-exploring hard ones. title: RIDGE: State-Conditioned Reward Blending for Behavioral Coverage in Deep RL Game Agents
description:
arXiv:2611.05601v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A deep RL agent trained on a fixed persona reward plays one way: an Explorer keeps exploring while starving, a Survivor hoards on an empty map. Since each persona fixes its own reward, automated playtesting trains N agents for N styles. description:
arXiv:2611.05390v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision. Yet a reviewer can both repair errors and replace decisions that were already correct. Abstract: Tiered inference distributes large language model computation across a hierarchy of devices, from on-device and edge hardware to the datacenter, and is increasingly offered as the route to cheaper, lower-latency, and more private serving.
